description: A four-panel composite figure mixing diffraction and property data. (a) and (b) are two stacked XRD patterns (y-axis "Intensity (a.u)", x-axis "2θ(degree)" from 40 to 120) each containing six traces labelled Hot Rolled, IA750_5 Min, IA750_30 Min, IA750_60 Min, IA750_120 Min and IA750_180 Min, with the header "α:ferrite (δ/α), γ:austenite" and indexed reflections α110, γ111, γ200, α200, γ220, α211, γ311 and γ222; the caption states (a) is before and (b) after tensile testing, but at the supplied resolution the two look nearly identical. (c) is a combined bar-and-line chart with a left axis "Volume fraction of austenite (%)" (0-50); black bars (Before tensile test) and red bars (After tensile test) are labelled 19/18, 46/42, 40/37, 35/28, 30/28 and 30/27 for HR, IA750_5Min, IA750_30Min, IA750_60Min, IA750_120Min and IA750_180Min; a blue line (Transformation Ratio of austenite, %) and a green line (Mechanical stability of austenite (K)) use right-hand axes. (d) plots YS and UTS ("Stress (MPa)", 400-700), TE (%) and PSE (GPa%) versus the same six conditions, with error bars. The group argues that IA750_60 Min gives the best balance of austenite fraction and stability, producing the maximum PSE.
measured_quantities: product of strength and elongation PSE (GPa%)

observations.observation: Panels (a) and (b) are XRD patterns plotted as Intensity (a.u) versus 2θ(degree) over the range 40-120°, with the header 'α:ferrite (δ/α), γ:austenite' and indexed reflections α110, γ111, γ200, α200, γ220, α211, γ311, γ222.
Both XRD panels contain the same six stacked traces, labelled from bottom to top: Hot Rolled, IA750_5 Min, IA750_30 Min, IA750_60 Min, IA750_120 Min, IA750_180 Min.

Panel (c) black bars are labelled 19, 46, 40, 35, 30, 30 and red bars 18, 42, 37, 28, 28, 27 for HR, IA750_5Min, IA750_30Min, IA750_60Min, IA750_120Min, IA750_180Min, i.e. austenite volume fraction decreases after the tensile test in every condition.
Panel (c) legend defines black as 'Before tensile test' and red as 'After tensile test'; the left axis is 'Volume fraction of austenite (%)' spanning 0-50.

In panel (c) the highest printed value on the green 'Mechanical stability of austenite (K)' line is 3.216 (near HR) and the lowest is 1.079 (near IA750_30Min), with printed values 1.929, 1.618 and 2.198 at other annealing times.

In panel (c) the blue 'Transformation Ratio of austenite (%)' line peaks at the IA750_60Min condition; the printed number at its apex is only partially legible and its value is not reliably readable from the supplied resolution.

Panel (d) shows TE (red squares, right axis 'TE(%)' 0-14) and PSE (blue squares, right axis 'PSE (GPa%)' 0-11) both rising to a maximum at IA750_60 Min and falling again for IA750_120 Min and IA750_180 Min.

Panel (d) shows UTS (black circles) highest at IA750_60 Min, sitting between the 650 and 700 MPa gridlines, while YS (black squares) is highest for Hot Rolled at just under the 500 MPa gridline and decreases across the annealed conditions.
The caption states that (a) is the XRD analysis of hot rolled & quenched (HRQ) and annealed specimens before tensile loading, and (b) the same specimens after the tensile test.

The caption states that panel (c) reports the volume fraction of austenite before and after the tensile test together with the mechanical stability (K) and the transformation rate of austenite in rolled & quenched and annealed specimens.
The caption states that panel (d) reports the mechanical performance of the developed steel in hot rolled & quenched and annealed condition.
The citing text states that the volume fraction of retained austenite (untransformed + reverted) before and after tensile deformation was measured by Rietveld analysis of the XRD data.
The citing text states that the mechanical stability of austenite was calculated using Sugimoto's model following eq (5).

The citing text states that as annealing time increases the austenite fraction decreases, confirmed by the austenite fraction from the XRD analysis in Fig. 7(c), and that in the IA750_180 Min specimen the needle/globular reverted austenite is almost completely dissolved into intercritical ferrite, leaving mostly intercritical ferrite (α) and untransformed austenite.

subfigures.description: Stacked XRD patterns of six conditions (Hot Rolled to IA750_180 Min) over 2θ = 40-120°, header 'α:ferrite (δ/α), γ:austenite', with reflections labelled α110, γ111, γ200, α200, γ220, α211, γ311, γ222. Caption states this is the before-tensile-loading state; two-theta positions of α110 (~44.7°), α200 (~65°) and α211 (~82°) are visible.

Same stacked XRD layout and labels as (a) for the same six conditions, stated by the caption to be after tensile testing. Visually almost identical to (a) at the supplied resolution; no clear peak-by-peak difference between the two can be resolved.

Bar chart with dual/right-hand line axes: black bars = 'Before tensile test', red bars = 'After tensile test' for the volume fraction of austenite (%), labelled 19/18, 46/42, 40/37, 35/28, 30/28, 30/27 across HR to IA750_180Min. A blue line (Transformation Ratio of austenite, %) peaks at IA750_60Min and a green line (Mechanical stability of austenite (K)) has printed labels including 3.216 (HR), 1.929, 1.079, 1.618 and 2.198.

Line plot with error bars of mechanical performance vs condition (Hot Rolled, IA750_5 Min ... IA750_180 Min): YS and UTS on the left 'Stress (MPa)' axis (400-700), TE (%) on the red right axis (0-14) and PSE (GPa%) on the blue right axis (0-11). TE and PSE both peak at IA750_60 Min; UTS also peaks there, while YS is highest for Hot Rolled.

unreadable_items: panels (a) and (b): the two XRD panels appear nearly identical at the supplied resolution, so any peak-intensity change before versus after the tensile test cannot be resolved from the pixels
panel (c): right-hand axis tick values (blue 'Transformation Ratio of austenite (%)' and green 'Mechanical stability of austenite (K)') are only partially legible
panel (c): the printed value at the apex of the blue curve at IA750_60Min is not reliably legible
panel (d): individual numeric values are not printed; only gridline-level estimates of YS/UTS/TE/PSE are possible
